questions.q: What does the accounting equation state?
questions.explain: Every correct entry keeps it balanced.

questions.q: What is the golden rule for personal accounts?
options: Debit what comes in, credit what goes out
Debit the giver, credit the receiver
Debit the receiver, credit the giver
questions.explain: Personal accounts are people and organisations such as Ramesh or HDFC Bank.

questions.q: The owner starts the business with ₹5,00,000 cash. What is the entry?
options: Purchases A/c Dr / To Capital A/c
Capital A/c Dr / To Cash A/c
Bank A/c Dr / To Cash A/c
Cash A/c Dr / To Capital A/c
questions.explain: Cash comes in (real account, debit) and Capital is the giver (personal account, credit).

questions.q: You buy stationery stock on credit from Lakshmi Paper Mart for ₹80,000. What is the entry?
options: Purchases A/c Dr / To Lakshmi Paper Mart
Lakshmi Paper Mart Dr / To Purchases A/c
Purchases A/c Dr / To Cash A/c
Cash A/c Dr / To Purchases A/c
questions.explain: Purchases is a nominal expense (debit) and the supplier is the giver (credit).

questions.q: What is the limit in Educational Mode?
options: Voucher dates are limited to the 1st, 2nd and 31st of a month
questions.explain: All features work, which is enough for learning.

questions.q: Which shortcut opens a search box from anywhere in TallyPrime?
questions.explain: Type 'Ledger', 'Sales' or 'Balance Sheet' and press Enter.

questions.q: How do you accept or save a screen?
questions.explain: Esc goes back, and Alt+C creates a master while inside a voucher.

questions.q: A TallyVault password is set on the company. What should you remember?
options: It encrypts the data and cannot be recovered if forgotten
It is optional and unrelated to data
It can be reset by Tally support
questions.explain: Never forget it.

questions.q: What does a ledger's group decide?
options: Where the ledger appears (Balance Sheet or Profit & Loss) and how it behaves
questions.explain: Every ledger belongs to a group.

questions.q: Under which group does a customer like Vijay Book Stall belong?
questions.explain: Suppliers go under Sundry Creditors.

questions.q: What happens if you classify freight inward as an indirect expense?
options: Net profit is understated by tax
questions.explain: Direct expenses affect gross profit; indirect expenses affect net profit.

questions.q: Which two ledgers exist by default?
questions.explain: Cash sits under Cash-in-Hand.

questions.q: You deposit ₹40,000 cash into HDFC Bank. Which voucher?
questions.explain: Contra records transfers between cash and bank accounts only.

questions.q: You pay rent of ₹15,000 from HDFC Bank. Which voucher?
questions.explain: Money is going out of the bank.

questions.q: Which entry is recorded in a Journal voucher?
options: Depreciation on a computer, with no cash or bank involved
questions.explain: Rule of thumb: cash/bank involved means Payment, Receipt or Contra; otherwise Journal.

questions.q: Why always write a narration?
options: Auditors and your future self need to understand the transaction
questions.explain: Narration explains each entry.

questions.q: Which function key opens a Sales voucher and which a Purchase voucher?
options: F8 for Sales and F9 for Purchase
questions.explain: F4 Contra, F5 Payment, F6 Receipt, F7 Journal, F8 Sales, F9 Purchase.

questions.q: How do you switch a voucher from accounting invoice to item invoice mode?
options: Ctrl+H (Change Mode), with Maintain Inventory on
questions.explain: Item invoice mode picks stock items, quantities and rates.

questions.q: A sale of 200 notebooks at ₹45 and 100 pen boxes at ₹60 totals what?
Why enter the supplier invoice number and date on a purchase voucher?
options: It's important for GST and payments later
questions.explain: The bill number links payments and GST records.

questions.q: What does a compound unit such as 'Box of 10 Nos' let you do?
options: Sell in boxes and track pieces
questions.explain: Simple units are Nos, Box, Kg, Pcs and Ream.

questions.q: A stock item has opening quantity 500 at ₹38. What is its opening value?
Which voucher records the actual counted quantities so book stock matches reality?
questions.explain: TallyPrime adjusts book stock to match the count.

questions.q: What is the default stock valuation method?
questions.explain: Other methods are set per item in Level 3.

questions.q: Why can books and bank statements differ on a given day?
options: Uncleared cheques, unrecorded bank charges or interest, direct deposits and errors
questions.explain: Reconciliation explains every difference.

questions.q: Bank charges of ₹590 include ₹500 plus 18% GST. How much is the GST?
For each entry that appears in the bank statement, what do you enter in the reconciliation screen?
options: The Bank Date, the date the bank processed it
questions.explain: Entries without a bank date stay unreconciled.

questions.q: How often should you reconcile?
options: At least monthly, ideally weekly for active accounts
questions.explain: Frequent reconciliation keeps differences small.

questions.q: What must be true of a Trial Balance?
questions.explain: A 'Difference in opening balances' line means opening balances don't agree.

questions.q: Which Trial Balance entry should look suspicious?
options: A customer with a debit balance
questions.explain: A credit balance in cash is impossible; also scan for suppliers with debit balances.

questions.q: How is Gross Profit computed in the example?
options: Sales + closing stock minus opening stock, purchases and direct expenses
questions.explain: The example gives cost of goods sold ₹78,700 and gross profit ₹56,300.

questions.q: Which report lists who owes how much?
questions.explain: It lists all customers with balances.

questions.q: Sri Sai Traders buys notebooks with ₹500 GST and sells them with ₹700 GST. What does it pay the government?
questions.explain: Output tax ₹700 minus input tax credit ₹500.

questions.q: A Telangana seller sells to a customer in Hyderabad. Which tax applies?
questions.explain: Intra-state supply splits the tax into Central and State parts.

questions.q: A Telangana seller sells to Bengaluru, Karnataka. Which tax applies?
questions.explain: Inter-state supply attracts IGST.

questions.q: Who ultimately bears the GST?
options: The final consumer, with businesses acting as collectors
questions.explain: Businesses collect output tax and claim input tax credit.

questions.q: Why does the Level 1 project use amounts excluding tax?
questions.explain: The month's transactions are recorded without GST.

questions.q: How do you record the owner's capital with ₹4,50,000 in the bank and ₹1,50,000 in cash?
options: Capital credited ₹6,00,000, with bank and cash debited accordingly (using a Contra for the deposit)
questions.explain: The brief says ₹4,50,000 deposited in Canara Bank and ₹1,50,000 cash.

questions.q: How should 2 damaged tawas found in the physical count be recorded?
options: Through a Stock Journal to a 'Damaged Stock' item, or as a loss
questions.explain: The project lists this as transaction 12.

questions.q: Why assume the ₹60,000 cheque hasn't been presented in the reconciliation?
options: To practise treating cheques issued but not yet presented as a reconciling difference
questions.explain: It appears in the books but not yet in the bank statement.

questions.q: Where do you enable GST for a company?
options: F11 (Company Features), set Enable Goods and Services Tax to Yes
questions.explain: Then enter state, registration type and GSTIN.

questions.q: Under which group are GST tax ledgers created?
questions.explain: With Type of duty/tax set to GST and the matching tax type.

questions.q: Why leave the percentage blank on tax ledgers?
options: TallyPrime picks the rate from the item or ledger GST details
questions.explain: GST rates are best set on stock items.

questions.q: What do the first digits of a GSTIN such as 37ABCDE1234F1Z9 identify?
questions.explain: TallyPrime also validates the GSTIN format.

questions.q: An intra-state sale of ₹12,000 at 18% shows what tax and invoice total?
questions.explain: 9% CGST + 9% SGST on 12,000.

questions.q: An inter-state sale of ₹35,000 at 18% IGST has what total?
questions.explain: IGST is 6,300.

questions.q: When is a Bill of Supply used instead of a tax invoice?
options: When no tax is charged, e.g. by composition dealers or for exempt goods
questions.explain: A tax invoice carries tax details.

questions.q: Where does TallyPrime take Place of Supply from by default?
options: From the party's state, changeable if goods are delivered elsewhere
questions.explain: For example 'bill to' one state and 'ship to' another.

questions.q: Which is a condition for claiming ITC?
options: The supplier has reported the invoice so it appears in your GSTR-2B
questions.explain: You also need a valid tax invoice, receipt of goods or services, tax paid by the supplier and a filed GSTR-3B.

questions.q: If you don't pay the supplier within 180 days, what happens to the ITC?
options: It must be reversed with interest and can be re-claimed when paid
questions.explain: This is one of the claim conditions.

questions.q: What is GSTR-2B?
options: A static monthly statement showing ITC available from suppliers' filings
questions.explain: It's generated around the 14th and shows ITC available and not available.

questions.q: What does the Invoice Management System (IMS) let you do?
options: Accept, reject or keep pending inward invoices before GSTR-2B is finalised
questions.explain: Review it monthly.

questions.q: What do GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B contain?
options: GSTR-1 details of sales; GSTR-3B summary and payment
questions.explain: Every regular taxpayer files both.

questions.q: Even with no activity in a month, what should a taxpayer do?
options: File on time (nil returns can be filed by SMS)
questions.explain: Late fees and interest apply otherwise.

questions.q: What should you resolve before exporting GSTR-1 from TallyPrime?
options: Uncertain transactions such as missing GSTIN, HSN, place of supply or rate
questions.explain: They appear in the return view.

questions.q: In tax set-off, which credit is used first?
options: IGST credit against IGST liability, then CGST and SGST
questions.explain: The worked example sets off IGST credit first.

questions.q: How do you correct an issued GST invoice's tax value?
options: Issue a credit or debit note; never edit the issued invoice
questions.explain: Credit notes reduce value and debit notes increase it.

questions.q: A customer returns 5 kadais at ₹600 with 18% GST. What does the credit note total?
questions.explain: ₹3,000 plus ₹270 CGST and ₹270 SGST.

questions.q: Why select the original invoice number and date in the credit note?
options: Reference details are required for GST reporting
questions.explain: It links the credit note to the invoice.

questions.q: A discount that wasn't agreed before supply or linked to invoices should be recorded how?
options: As a commercial credit note without GST
questions.explain: Such discounts don't reduce GST value.

questions.q: What does the IRP return when an e-invoice is registered?
options: An IRN (Invoice Reference Number), acknowledgement details and a signed QR code
questions.explain: TallyPrime stores and prints them on the invoice.

questions.q: Which invoices does e-invoicing apply to?
options: B2B invoices, exports and credit/debit notes to registered persons, not B2C
questions.explain: B2C may need a dynamic QR code above a higher threshold.

questions.q: Within what time can an IRN be cancelled?
options: 24 hours; afterwards issue a credit note
questions.explain: Cancel on the IRP, then in TallyPrime.

questions.q: What are Part A and Part B of an e-way bill?
options: A: supplier/recipient and invoice details; B: transporter and vehicle details
questions.explain: Validity is generally 1 day per 200 km for regular cargo.

questions.q: What is the reverse charge mechanism?
options: The recipient pays the GST instead of the supplier
questions.explain: It applies to notified goods and services and some imports of services.

questions.q: How must tax under RCM be paid?
options: In cash (electronic cash ledger), not with ITC
With a cheque to the supplier
questions.explain: The recipient can then claim the same amount as ITC if eligible.

questions.q: Advocate fees of ₹50,000 at 18% intra-state under RCM create what liability?
questions.explain: The recipient pays ₹9,000 in cash and claims ₹9,000 ITC.

questions.q: Where is RCM liability reported in GSTR-3B?
questions.explain: Liability and ITC are reported separately.

questions.q: What does 'Agst Ref' mean?
options: A payment or receipt against an existing bill
questions.explain: New Ref is a new bill; Advance is money before an invoice; On Account isn't linked to a bill.

questions.q: A receipt of ₹70,000 settles invoice A (₹59,000) fully and invoice B (₹35,400) partly. How much of B is pending?
What does ageing analysis group pending bills by?
options: Age buckets such as 0–30, 31–60, 61–90 and 90+ days
questions.explain: It identifies risky debts.

questions.q: Why does paying suppliers by due date matter for GST?
options: It keeps credit terms and meets the 180-day rule for ITC
questions.explain: Otherwise ITC may need reversing.

questions.q: What do cost centres tell you beyond total profit?
options: Which branch, department, project or salesperson drove it
questions.explain: A cost category is a dimension and cost centres sit under it.

questions.q: How can one voucher allocate sales by both branch and salesperson?
options: Use different cost categories in the same voucher
questions.explain: Branches and Salespeople are separate categories.

questions.q: What does a cost centre class do?
options: Applies a fixed allocation automatically, such as salary split 50/30/20
questions.explain: It saves repeated manual allocation.

questions.q: How do you compare actual results with a budget?
options: Add the budget variance column in Trial Balance, Group Summary or Cost Centre reports
questions.explain: It shows variance and percentage; review monthly.

questions.q: Which entry in the wholesaler project is paid in cash through the electronic cash ledger?
questions.explain: The project includes advocate fees and GTA freight under RCM.

questions.q: Why does the project create a GSTR-2B with one mismatch and one supplier non-filer?
options: To practise reconciling purchases and deciding actions such as holding back ITC
questions.explain: The summary must say how much ITC is held back and why.

questions.q: Which sales does the project make for GSTR-1 classification practice?
options: Intra-state B2B, inter-state B2B, B2C retail and an inter-state B2C above ₹1 lakh
questions.explain: The large inter-state B2C one is reported individually.

questions.q: What must the set-off journal and payment voucher reflect?
options: Set-off in the correct order and RCM paid in cash
questions.explain: It follows the GSTR-3B computation.

questions.q: What is TDS?
options: Tax deducted by the payer from certain payments and deposited with the government
questions.explain: Examples: contractor bills, professional fees, rent, commission and salaries.

questions.q: What happens if the payee gives no valid PAN?
options: TDS generally applies at a higher rate, often 20%
questions.explain: Collect PAN before payment.

questions.q: By when is TDS generally deposited?
options: The 7th of the following month (30 April for March)
questions.explain: Quarterly statements follow on fixed dates.

questions.q: What do you need in order to deduct TDS?
questions.explain: TallyPrime asks for TAN when you enable TDS.

questions.q: How does TCS differ from TDS?
options: TCS is collected by the seller from the buyer; TDS is deducted by the payer
TCS is deducted by the buyer
questions.explain: Both are deposited with the government.

questions.q: What GST TCS rate do e-commerce operators collect on net taxable supplies?
questions.explain: They report it in GSTR-8, and it appears in the seller's cash ledger.

questions.q: Where is a TCS payable ledger created?
options: Under Duties & Taxes with Type TCS
questions.explain: Set TCS applicability on the buyer ledger and sales ledger or item.

questions.q: When is income-tax TCS collected?
options: At the time of receipt or debit to the buyer
questions.explain: Deposit by the 7th of the following month and file quarterly statements.

questions.q: What is the employee's EPF contribution rate in the lesson?
questions.explain: The employer also contributes 12%, split between EPF and pension.

questions.q: What are the ESI contribution rates in the lesson?
options: Employee 0.75% and employer 3.25% of gross wages
questions.explain: ESI applies to employees earning up to ₹21,000 a month.

questions.q: Which voucher records daily attendance in TallyPrime payroll?
questions.explain: The Payroll voucher then calculates earnings and deductions with auto fill.

questions.q: What are pay heads?
options: Components of salary such as Basic, HRA and deductions like PF
questions.explain: They define earnings and deductions.

questions.q: How do you move 100 fans from the Main Warehouse to Nashik Depot?
questions.explain: Godown Summary shows stock by location afterward.

questions.q: With opening 100 @ ₹1,800, a purchase of 200 @ ₹1,950 and 220 sold, what is the FIFO closing stock?
questions.explain: FIFO sells the older 100 @ 1,800 first, then 120 @ 1,950, leaving 80 @ 1,950.

questions.q: What is the weighted-average cost per unit in that example?
What does FEFO mean for perishables?
questions.explain: Select batches on sale by earliest expiry.

questions.q: What does a Bill of Materials define?
options: The components needed per unit of a finished item
questions.explain: For one study table: plywood, legs, screws, laminate and drawer runners.

questions.q: Producing 20 tables needs 4 legs each. How many legs?
How is the finished goods cost computed?
options: (Components + additional costs such as labour and power) ÷ quantity
questions.explain: For 20 tables: components plus ₹12,000 labour and ₹3,000 power.

questions.q: Under GST, how do goods move for job work?
options: On a delivery challan without tax, returning within 1 year (inputs) or 3 years (capital goods)
questions.explain: Otherwise it's treated as a supply; movements are reported in ITC-04.

questions.q: How does TallyPrime print a cheque?
options: In a Payment voucher choose transaction type Cheque; it picks the next number and prints the amount in words
questions.explain: Enable cheque printing in the bank ledger first.

questions.q: What do post-dated cheques do until their date?
options: They don't affect balances until the date; Post-Dated Summary lists upcoming items
questions.explain: On the due date the voucher becomes regular automatically.

questions.q: What is a maker-checker control in e-payments?
options: One person creates the payments, another approves the upload in net banking
questions.explain: It reduces payment fraud and errors.

questions.q: What does the Payment Advice report send to parties?
options: Details of payments made, such as invoices settled and TDS deducted
questions.explain: Email it with Alt+M.

questions.q: 500 fans at $28 with an exchange rate of ₹84.50 gives what invoice value?
The customer pays $14,000 when the rate is ₹85.10. What exchange gain?
questions.explain: 14,000 × (85.10 − 84.50) = 8,400, booked as forex gain under Indirect Incomes.

questions.q: What are the two GST routes for exporting goods?
options: Under LUT without paying IGST, or with IGST paid then refunded
questions.explain: Exports are zero-rated supplies.

questions.q: How is customs duty treated for imports?
options: It becomes part of inventory cost (IGST on imports is claimable as ITC)
questions.explain: The Bill of Entry gives the IGST paid.

questions.q: March electricity of ₹14,000 is incurred but unpaid. What is the entry?
questions.explain: Outstanding expenses are a current liability.

questions.q: Insurance ₹36,000 paid for July–June leaves how much prepaid at 31 March?
questions.explain: April–June is 3 of 12 months: 36,000 × 3/12.

questions.q: A 5% provision on ₹3,20,000 of debts over 90 days is how much?
questions.explain: It's booked as Dr Bad Debts / Cr Provision for doubtful debts.

questions.q: What is the depreciation entry in a Journal voucher?
options: Dr Depreciation (Indirect Expenses) / Cr the asset
questions.explain: Maintain a fixed asset register with cost, additions, disposals and depreciation.

questions.q: What is GSTR-9C?
options: A self-certified reconciliation between audited financial statements and GSTR-9, for larger taxpayers
questions.explain: It's required above the lesson's turnover threshold of ₹5 crore.

questions.q: What do composition taxpayers file instead?
questions.explain: E-commerce operators file GSTR-9B.

questions.q: How should you handle an additional liability discovered while preparing GSTR-9?
options: Pay it with interest through DRC-03 before filing
questions.explain: Compare TallyPrime's figures with GSTR-1, GSTR-3B and the portal.

questions.q: How long should GST records be kept?
options: At least 72 months from the due date of the annual return
questions.explain: Keep invoices, notes, e-way bills, challans, ITC documents and payment proofs.

questions.q: By when are PF/ESI payments made in the project?
questions.explain: TDS deposits are by the 7th.

questions.q: Which transaction combines import, customs duty and IGST in the project?
options: A raw material purchase in USD
questions.explain: Customs duty becomes part of inventory cost; IGST on imports is claimable.

questions.q: Why does the project include a scrap sale?
questions.explain: TCS applies to specified sales such as scrap.

questions.q: What does the close include after adjustments?
options: Stock verification, bank reconciliation, GST returns and a management report pack
questions.explain: The deliverable checklist lists them all.

questions.q: Sales 600, COGS 450. What is the gross profit margin?
Current assets 180 (stock 90) and current liabilities 110. What is the quick ratio?
What does the cash conversion cycle of 72 days mean?
options: Each rupee of sales is tied up for over two months
questions.explain: DSO 46 + inventory days 73 − creditor days 47.

questions.q: Why can a profitable business still run out of cash?
options: Profit isn't cash: stock and debtors tie cash up, so check the cash flow report
questions.explain: Compare cash from operations with profit.

questions.q: What does an MIS summary dashboard show?
options: Revenue, gross margin %, net profit, cash and bank, receivables, payables and stock, with change vs last month and budget
questions.explain: It is a one-page view.

questions.q: How is a cash flow forecast built?
options: Opening cash + expected receipts (including post-dated cheques) − planned payments
questions.explain: Planned payments include suppliers, salaries, GST, TDS and EMIs.

questions.q: When should the monthly MIS pack be delivered?
options: Within the first 5–7 working days, after reconciliation
questions.explain: Keep definitions such as 'gross margin' consistent.

questions.q: What should accompany each section of the pack?
options: 2–3 bullets on what changed, why and the recommended action
questions.explain: Commentary drives action.

questions.q: What is segregation of duties?
options: The person who records purchases shouldn't approve payments or reconcile the bank
questions.explain: It reduces error and fraud.

questions.q: What does the edit log record?
options: Creation, alteration and deletion of vouchers and masters with user, date, time and previous versions
questions.explain: View it via Related Reports → Edit Log.

questions.q: Why lock periods after closing?
options: So no one alters closed periods; changes need administrator unlock and leave a trace
questions.explain: For example lock up to 31 March after audit.

questions.q: Which role can create vouchers only?
questions.explain: An Auditor can only view.

questions.q: What is the 3-2-1 backup rule?
questions.explain: For example encrypted cloud storage as the off-site copy.

questions.q: Why test restores regularly?
options: A backup you can't restore isn't a backup
questions.explain: Restore to a different path first if unsure.

questions.q: What must you do before repairing or splitting a company?
questions.explain: Then verify closing balances equal opening balances in the new company after a split.

questions.q: Why should you never copy company files while TallyPrime has the company open?
options: Use TallyPrime's own backup tools instead
questions.explain: Files may be inconsistent while open.

questions.q: By which day is monthly GSTR-1 due and by which is GSTR-3B?
options: GSTR-1 by the 20th, GSTR-3B by the 11th
GSTR-1 by the 11th and GSTR-3B by the 20th
questions.explain: TDS/TCS is deposited by the 7th and PF/ESI by the 15th.

questions.q: Which are the quarterly TDS statement due dates?
questions.explain: 15 June, 15 September, 15 December and 15 March are advance tax instalments.

questions.q: When is GSTR-9/9C due?
questions.explain: It follows the financial year.

questions.q: How should you run the calendar?
options: Recurring reminders 5 and 2 days before each deadline, with an owner and a backup
questions.explain: Maintain a compliance tracker.

questions.q: Which structure has limited liability with lighter compliance than a company?
questions.explain: A private limited company is a separate legal entity with more compliance.

questions.q: A founder lends money to the company without being issued shares. How is it recorded?
options: As an unsecured loan with documentation, not capital
questions.explain: Personal expenses through the business are recorded as drawings.

questions.q: ₹60 lakh cash with ₹5 lakh monthly net burn gives what runway?
questions.explain: Runway is cash balance ÷ net burn.

questions.q: What is the maximum period for a buyer to pay an MSME supplier?
questions.explain: The lesson notes delayed payment protection and tracking MSME status in ledgers.

questions.q: Which is a sign you may need more than TallyPrime alone?
options: Many users across locations needing real-time access, complex approvals, MRP or multi-company consolidation
questions.explain: Moving is a business decision, not a default.

questions.q: How should you evaluate an ERP?
options: Prioritized requirements, 5-year total cost of ownership and demos using your own scenarios
questions.explain: Check partner experience and people readiness too.

questions.q: What do you do before migrating from TallyPrime?
options: Clean the data: remove duplicate ledgers, fix groupings and close old bills
questions.explain: Choose a cut-over date, usually a financial year or quarter start.

questions.q: Which system does the lesson pair with cloud-first SMEs and startups?
questions.explain: S/4HANA and Fusion are for large enterprises.

questions.q: Which services are reserved for Chartered Accountants or other authorised professionals?
options: Statutory audits, tax audits and certification, among others
questions.explain: Check what you're allowed to offer.

questions.q: What does an engagement letter set out?
options: Scope, client responsibilities, timelines, fees, payment terms, confidentiality and limitations
questions.explain: It protects both sides.

questions.q: How should client data be handled?
options: Secure remote access, encryption on personal devices, backups and clear data-return terms
questions.explain: DPDP obligations apply to personal data.

questions.q: Why niche by industry?
options: To work faster and market better
questions.explain: For example restaurants, traders, clinics or startups.

questions.q: Which role leads a team and owns budgeting, cash flow and banking relationships?
questions.explain: The CFO/Financial Controller role adds strategy, funding and governance.

questions.q: Which skills do employers look for?
options: TallyPrime with GST/TDS/payroll, end-to-end GST, advanced Excel and month-end discipline
questions.explain: ERP exposure helps for larger companies.

questions.q: How should resume achievements read?
options: Results-focused, e.g. reconciled GSTR-2B monthly and recovered missed ITC
questions.explain: Quantify honestly.

questions.q: How should you build a portfolio from the course?
options: Use screenshots only of the home page
Use the projects with exported reports (monthly books, GST month, quarter-end close, full-year capstone)
questions.explain: Practical experience matters as much as certificates.

questions.q: How much of the year does the capstone require you to record in full?
options: At least one representative month per quarter, summarising the others
questions.explain: There are four representative months.

questions.q: Which year-end items does the capstone include?
options: Adjustments, forex restatement, GSTR-9 reconciliation and ITC reversals for unpaid suppliers
questions.explain: It ends by locking the year, backing up and splitting.

questions.q: What controls are set at the start?
options: Security roles, the edit log, a backup policy and a compliance calendar
questions.explain: Part of setup in the brief.

questions.q: What does the annual MIS report include?
questions.explain: It sits in the deliverables checklist.

questions.q: The owner puts ₹5,00,000 cash into a new business. What is the entry?
options: Capital A/c Dr / To Cash A/c
Purchases A/c Dr / To Cash A/c
Bank A/c Dr / To Capital A/c
Cash A/c Dr / To Capital A/c
questions.explain: Cash comes in (debit) and Capital is the giver (credit).

questions.q: You deposit cash into the bank. Which voucher type?
questions.explain: Contra covers transfers between cash and bank.

questions.q: An adjustment such as depreciation, with no cash or bank, needs which voucher?
questions.explain: Rule of thumb: cash/bank involved → Payment/Receipt/Contra, otherwise Journal.

questions.q: A customer's account shows a credit balance and a supplier's shows a debit balance in the Trial Balance. What should you do?
options: Investigate: these oddities suggest wrong entries or overpayment
questions.explain: Scan for oddities after confirming debits equal credits.

questions.q: You sell from Telangana to a registered buyer in Karnataka at 18%. Which tax is charged?
questions.explain: Inter-state supply attracts IGST.

questions.q: Your purchase invoice from a supplier doesn't appear in GSTR-2B. What should you do with the ITC?
options: Hold it back until the supplier reports it, and follow up
questions.explain: ITC requires the supplier to have reported the invoice.

questions.q: You issued an invoice with the wrong quantity. How do you correct it under GST?
options: Issue a credit or debit note referencing the original invoice
questions.explain: Never edit an issued invoice's tax value.

questions.q: Your turnover is above ₹5 crore and you raise a B2B sale. What must you do?
options: Report it to the IRP and get an IRN, with a QR code on the invoice
questions.explain: E-invoicing applies to B2B invoices above the threshold.

questions.q: You hire an advocate and pay ₹50,000 plus 18% GST under reverse charge. Who pays the GST and how?
options: You, in cash through the electronic cash ledger, then claim ITC if eligible
questions.explain: RCM tax must be paid in cash.

questions.q: A customer pays ₹70,000 against two open invoices. Which entry type pairs payment to bills?
questions.explain: Agst Ref settles specific bills.

questions.q: You must see profit by branch and by salesperson. What do you use?
questions.explain: Allocate in vouchers and use Cost Centre reports.

questions.q: You pay a contractor ₹1,00,000 and the payee has no PAN. What generally applies?
questions.explain: Invalid or missing PAN triggers a higher rate.

questions.q: By when is TDS deducted in a month generally deposited?
questions.explain: For March it is 30 April.

questions.q: Copper wire: opening 100 @ ₹1,800, purchase 200 @ ₹1,950, 220 sold. Under FIFO, what is the cost of goods sold?
You send tables to a polishing unit. How do you move the goods under GST?
options: Delivery challan without tax, with Material Out/In vouchers
questions.explain: Track return within the allowed time and report ITC-04.

questions.q: A foreign customer pays at a better exchange rate than the invoice rate. How is the difference treated?
options: As an exchange gain under Indirect Incomes
questions.explain: Book it with a forex gain/loss adjustment.

questions.q: It is year end. March electricity of ₹14,000 hasn't been paid. What do you book?
questions.explain: An adjusting entry for an expense incurred but not paid.

questions.q: A profitable business is short of cash. Which ratios and reports help you diagnose it?
options: Cash conversion cycle, debtor days and the cash flow report
questions.explain: Profit isn't cash; stock and debtors tie it up.

questions.q: Your accounting data is on one PC. What is the safe backup approach?
options: One copy on the same disk
3 copies, on 2 media, 1 off-site (e.g. encrypted cloud), with tested restores
questions.explain: A backup you can't restore isn't a backup.

questions.q: A junior accountant records purchases and also approves payments and reconciles the bank. What is the control weakness?
questions.explain: Separate recording, approval and reconciliation, and use the edit log.
